changes.text: The `header` snippet receives `titleId` (`Snippet<[string]>`): put it on your heading (`id={titleId}`) so a custom header keeps the dialog named. Snippets that ignore the argument keep working, with `title` / `aria-label` used as an `aria-label` fallback and a dev `console.warn` when the dialog ends up unnamed.

The page behind no longer scrolls while the dialog is open: `<html>` gets `overflow: hidden` through a reference-counted lock (`data-ss-scroll-lock`), and `.body` uses `overscroll-behavior: contain`. Plain-HTML dialogs driven by `dssoca/vanilla.js` lock and release the same way.
`lockScroll` / `unlockScroll` are exported from `dssoca/vanilla.js`: the scroll lock shared with `SearchPalette`, safe for stacked dialogs.
The close button is pushed to the inline end with `margin-inline-start: auto` (was `margin-left`), so it sits on the correct side under `dir="rtl"`.

Plain-HTML behaviour in `dssoca/vanilla.js` for `<dialog class="ss-modal">` markup: `data-ss-modal="#id"` openers, `data-ss-dismiss` closers and backdrop click to close. `data-ss-static` on the dialog disables backdrop close and `data-ss-no-esc` blocks Escape, mirroring `closeOnBackdrop` / `closeOnEsc`.

New `fullscreen` prop (default `false`) fills the viewport instead of rendering a centred, capped panel: header and footer stay pinned and the body owns the scroll. It renders `data-fullscreen` on the dialog; in this mode `size` has no effect on width and `closeOnBackdrop` is unreachable, so the close button and Esc are the exits.

New component: a dialog built on the native `<dialog>` element, with a focus trap, `Esc` and backdrop close (`closeOnEsc`, `closeOnBackdrop`), a bindable `open`, `title`, `size`, `header` / `footer` snippets, `onclose` and a `danger` styling hint.
